items.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024
items.q: I think it’s from Pat Metheny, he said, “Everybody has about seven or eight tunes in them...”

ctx.x: You improvised the melody? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Well not complet — I mean I kind of came up with this little descending line and then I tinkered with it. So when I improvised it it wasn’t in its final form but I just kind of came up with that melody as a result of hearing the ostinato in the chords. And I mean these days there’s a — I think it’s from Pat Metheny, he said, “Everybody has about seven or eight tunes in them and they keep writing different versions of that same tune.” So I’m getting to that point where I’m repeating myself, or I feel like I’m…

Like I can totally relate to that. Because I usually start at the piano myself and like I’m not a fantastic piano player so I do find that I’m trying to put my hands down in different ways. Like, and you mentioned bass notes, like instead of thinking before your hands hit, okay I’m going to do some E flat thing, like just put your hands down and see what happens.
